next_objective.constraints: Use a spare/bench setup with a recovery plan and a legitimate load path. Do not alter the vehicle, production radio, safety policy, firmware image, signing path, MFi authentication or projection protocol. This objective proves only the transport primitive.
next_objective.success: On owner-authorized spare/bench hardware, capture the existing host controller and hub path issuing AOA Get Protocol/string/start requests, observe Google accessory VID/PID re-enumeration, claim the bulk IN/OUT endpoints, and exchange bounded deterministic frames in both directions with clean detach/recovery.
next_objective.title: Prove AOA negotiation and bidirectional bulk I/O through the stock RA4 cabin USB path

android_auto.blocker: The first blocker is not Internet service or USB device mode; it is proving that a production-compatible RA4 host client can take a phone from normal enumeration through AOA re-enumeration and exchange bidirectional bulk frames without losing the stock cabin path.
android_auto.conclusion: A software prototype is technically plausible because RA4 is already a true USB host with the vendor-control, descriptor and bulk primitives AOA needs, and its display/HMI/audio foundations are substantial. Significant unknowns remain: stock-path AOA ownership, a legitimate receiver, installed H.264 decode, PCM/microphone contracts and measured resources.

carplay.blocker: Before receiver work, identify a compatible Apple authentication IC and its legitimate integration path, then prove that the active media hub and Radio C2 route can reverse roles with supported VBUS behavior. An existing legacy iPod path is not sufficient evidence.
carplay.conclusion: CarPlay is silicon-plausible but requires hardware-backed MFi authentication and, on the documented QNX 6.6 path, a reversible cabin USB route plus a device-side controller stack. None is proved present or compatible on RA4; licensed receiver software is also missing.
